FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A38
Operating another person’s vehicle without consent while intending only to deprive the owner temporarily, rather than steal it, is a misdemeanor. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A38
A mechanically unsafe vehicle must not be driven in Idaho. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A38
The driver is responsible for correcting dangerous defects, missing essential equipment or necessary vehicle repairs. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A38
Idaho does not require a yearly vehicle safety inspection. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A38
An officer who stops a vehicle and finds unsafe conditions or missing required equipment may issue a citation. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A38
A vehicle must have two independent brake systems so one remains usable if the other fails. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A38
On dry pavement, the foot brake must stop a vehicle traveling twenty miles an hour within twenty-five feet. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A38
At twenty miles an hour on dry pavement, the emergency or parking brake must stop the vehicle within fifty-five feet. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A38
The parking brake must keep a parked vehicle from moving on a hill. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A38
A vehicle needs two headlamps providing both high and low beams. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A38
Headlamps must illuminate the road without dazzling approaching drivers. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A38
High beams must make people and vehicles visible at least three hundred fifty feet ahead. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A38
Low beams must illuminate at least one hundred feet of roadway ahead. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A38
Headlights must not be covered with material that is reflective, opaque or non-transparent. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A39
A motor vehicle’s working brake lights must be red or amber and visible at least one hundred feet behind in normal sunlight. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A39
Brake lights must illuminate when the foot brake is applied. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A39
Brake-light lenses should be kept clean. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A39
A vehicle built before January first, nineteen fifty-six needs at least one red rear light. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A39
Except for vehicles built before January first, nineteen fifty-six, a passenger motor vehicle needs two red rear lights, one on each side, visible from five hundred feet behind. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A39
A motor vehicle built after January first, nineteen fifty-five needs driver-controlled flashing electric signals for both left and right turns at front and rear, visible from one hundred feet. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A39
On a motor vehicle built after January first, nineteen fifty-five, the front electric turn signals must be white or amber. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A39
On a motor vehicle built after January first, nineteen fifty-five, the rear electric turn signals must be red or amber. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A39
Each tire should retain at least two thirty-seconds of an inch of tread. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A39
A motor vehicle must have a horn audible from at least two hundred feet. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A39
A horn producing an unreasonably loud or harsh sound is prohibited. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A40
Vehicle windows and windshields must use approved safety glass. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A40
Damaged window or windshield glass must be replaced when it obstructs the driver’s view. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A40
Windows and windshields must remain free of signs and stickers other than those required by law. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A40
Objects placed or hung inside the vehicle must not block the windows or windshield. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A40
Frost, snow, dirt and other visibility obstructions must be removed from vehicle glass. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A40
Window and windshield treatments must not create a mirrored surface or otherwise make the glass difficult to see through, even from outside. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A40
Every motor vehicle needs windshield wipers that remove rain, snow and other moisture. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A40
A motor vehicle’s rear-view mirror must provide a highway view extending at least two hundred feet behind. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A40
When a load or trailer blocks the usual view through the rear window, the vehicle needs an additional mirror on each side. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A40
A vehicle without a rear-view mirror needs both a left and a right side mirror. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A40
A motor vehicle must have a working muffler that prevents unusual or loud noise. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A40
Motor vehicles and trailers need fenders, wheel covers or flaps that prevent wheel-thrown material from reaching other vehicles. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A39
A trailer or semitrailer built on or after January first, nineteen fifty-six needs at least two red rear lamps, one on each side, visible from five hundred feet behind. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0039]

Misconceptions: Parking lights do not replace headlights when driving conditions require lights; a child-seat recommendation is distinct from the statutory age requirement.
Mnemonic: See, stop and secure is a teaching reminder for visibility, braking and occupant restraints.
Glossary: High and low beams light different distances; a parking brake holds the stopped car; an overhanging load extends beyond the vehicle.
Dynamic facts: dated credential access policies, local service details and fee amounts are kept as verification debt outside the knowledge blocks.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A41
Children aged six or younger traveling in a non-commercial vehicle must use approved child safety seats under the law applicable to cars built with safety belts after January first, nineteen sixty-six. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A41
A child safety seat must meet federal safety standards. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A41
The child must fit snugly within the safety seat’s own straps. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A41
The child safety seat must be secured to the vehicle. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A41
The child safety seat must be used on every trip. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A41
The handbook recommends reading both the child-seat instructions and the vehicle manual for height and weight limits and correct installation. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A41
The handbook recommends the rear seat for every child younger than thirteen. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A41
The handbook’s safety recommendations say never to place a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A41
Idaho requires occupants to wear whichever safety belts and shoulder straps were supplied for them as factory equipment in the motor vehicle. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A42
Safety belts help the driver keep control on winding or rough roads and during collision-avoidance maneuvers. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A42
Red and blue emergency lights are permitted only on emergency vehicles. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A42
Sirens, bells and whistles are listed as prohibited equipment for ordinary vehicles. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A42
A muffler cutout or bypass that increases exhaust noise is prohibited. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A42
A vehicle must not have more than two spotlights. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A42
A vehicle must not have more than two front auxiliary lights. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A42
A vehicle must not have more than two front fog lights. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A42
A vehicle must not have more than two cowl or fender lights. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A43
Headlamps and taillamps must be on between sunset and sunrise. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A43
Poor visibility also requires headlamps and taillamps when needed for safety. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A43
A driver must dim headlights five hundred feet before meeting another vehicle. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R21 | anchor: A43
A driver must dim headlights two hundred feet before overtaking another vehicle. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R22 | anchor: A43
When driving requires lights, the driver must use headlights rather than parking lights. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R23 | anchor: A43
Before driving, the driver must clear ice, snow and dirt from the windows to preserve visibility in every direction. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R24 | anchor: A43
Passengers and cargo must not block the driver’s view or interfere with vehicle operation. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R25 | anchor: A43
By day, a load extending at least four feet behind the vehicle must carry a red flag at its far end. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R26 | anchor: A43
The flag on a load projecting at least four feet behind must be at least eighteen inches square. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R27 | anchor: A43
At night, a load projecting at least four feet behind needs a red light visible from at least five hundred feet in place of the flag. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R28 | anchor: A43
A vehicle’s load must not project beyond the left fenders. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R29 | anchor: A43
A vehicle’s load may extend no more than six inches beyond the right fenders. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R30 | anchor: A43
Reckless driving with willful disregard for people or property is prohibited on both public roads and private property. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R31 | anchor: A43
A driver must give full attention to operating the vehicle safely. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R32 | anchor: A43
Failure to attend to safe vehicle operation can result in an inattentive-driving citation. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec04-R33 | anchor: A41
The handbook directs readers to the child-seat and vehicle instructions for installation using a seat belt or the LATCH system. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R34 | anchor: A41
LATCH means Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec04-R35 | anchor: A42
The handbook notes that ITD sometimes changes studded-tire season dates because of weather. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0042]
